purpose: Define a supervised agency operating overlay for SEIS briefs, pod ownership, review gates, evidence, and handoff without granting runtime authority.

agency.name: SEIS Creative Engineering Agency
agency.mission: Turn bounded SEIS briefs into coherent, evidence-backed product, design, engineering, AI, and delivery outcomes.

headcountModel.allocationBasis: Proposed company-wide employee allocation for agency planning.

units.name: Executive & Strategy
units.mandate: Company direction, portfolio strategy, architecture governance, and long-horizon planning.

units.name: Client, Product & Program Management
units.mandate: Client briefs, product management, program delivery, and measurable acceptance.

units.name: Creative Direction, Brand & Design
units.mandate: Brand systems, graphic design, visual direction, interaction, motion, and content craft.

units.name: Product, UX & Research
units.mandate: User research, product discovery, service design, accessibility, and evidence-led decisions.

units.name: Software Engineering
units.mandate: Apple-native, web, backend, full-stack, systems, and shared platform implementation.

units.name: AI, Data & Knowledge Systems
units.mandate: AI Core, model and provider routing, agent systems, data, retrieval, memory, and evaluation.

units.name: Platform, Security, QA & DevOps
units.mandate: Infrastructure, reliability, security, quality gates, release engineering, and incident readiness.

units.name: People, Finance, Legal, Marketing & Operations
units.mandate: People operations, finance, legal, communications, marketing, procurement, and company operations.

pods.name: Direction & Product
pods.mandate: Clarify the brief, protect scope, define acceptance, and keep the work tied to SEIS goals.

pods.name: Experience
pods.mandate: Shape the SEIS product feel, interaction model, accessibility, motion, and visual evidence.

pods.name: Engineering
pods.mandate: Deliver scoped Apple-native, web, full-stack, platform, and release engineering outputs.

pods.name: Intelligence & Automation
pods.mandate: Provide source-backed research, search, knowledge, cloud-readiness, and safe automation planning.

pods.name: Trust & Delivery
pods.mandate: Protect secrets, privacy, quality, regression safety, release evidence, and honest status.

roles.duty: Own boundaries, architecture decisions, decomposition, and rollback-aware plans.
Own briefs, requirements, acceptance criteria, roadmap slices, and launch readiness.
Keep decisions, status, evidence, backlog, and handoff records navigable.
Own visual language, product feel, design tokens, and interaction evidence.
Review usability, focus order, mobile ergonomics, and accessibility.
Prepare scoped implementation notes, validators, tests, and code review evidence.
Own CI, release, deployment planning, rollback, and operational runbooks.
Provide source provenance, prior-art notes, and evidence-backed technical decisions.
Plan local documentation, route, file, plugin, and knowledge indexing.
Prepare cloud, SSH, storage, sync, and provider-readiness boundaries.
Design idempotent workflows, ledgers, dry-runs, and human-approved automation gates.
Protect secrets, private-vault boundaries, permissions, threat posture, and approvals.
Own deterministic validators, smoke checks, regression evidence, and acceptance proof.

serviceCatalog.name: Brief framing and goal decomposition
serviceCatalog.output: Bounded agency brief with goal, scope, non-goals, acceptance, risks, and validation.
serviceCatalog.validation: Brief template contains every required field and names a repository boundary.

serviceCatalog.name: Architecture and ADR decision
serviceCatalog.output: Smallest safe architecture decision, affected paths, dependencies, and rollback.
serviceCatalog.validation: Decision identifies canonical owner, boundaries, and a reproducible validation command.

serviceCatalog.name: Product design, UI/UX, and accessibility
serviceCatalog.output: Token-driven interaction proposal or implementation with accessible states and evidence.
serviceCatalog.validation: Keyboard, focus, contrast, responsive, and reduced-motion considerations are recorded.

serviceCatalog.name: Apple-native and platform engineering
serviceCatalog.output: Scoped Swift, SwiftUI, package, platform, or contract change.
serviceCatalog.validation: Relevant package or platform checks run, with unavailable toolchains disclosed.

serviceCatalog.name: Web and full-stack engineering
serviceCatalog.output: Scoped frontend, backend, API, data, or demo-surface change.
serviceCatalog.validation: Targeted tests, route checks, and public/private boundary checks run.

serviceCatalog.name: AI, agent, knowledge, and research planning
serviceCatalog.output: Source-backed AI or knowledge design with explicit maturity and non-claims.
serviceCatalog.validation: Sources, privacy class, provider status, evaluation path, and fallback are documented.

serviceCatalog.name: Cloud, SSH, and automation readiness
serviceCatalog.output: Readiness plan, dry-run, runbook, or rollback-aware infrastructure contract.
serviceCatalog.validation: No live mutation occurs; approval requirements, endpoint constraints, and rollback are explicit.

serviceCatalog.name: Security, privacy, and permission review
serviceCatalog.output: Threat, secret, permission, public/private, and approval review.
serviceCatalog.validation: Required security checks pass or the blocker is recorded with an unblock condition.

serviceCatalog.name: Quality, release, and handoff
serviceCatalog.output: Validation evidence, failed/skipped checks, release note, rollback, and next decision.
serviceCatalog.validation: Evidence is reproducible, status is honest, and the worktree state is reported.

workflow.name: Intake
workflow.output: A complete brief or an explicit clarification request.
workflow.gate: No implementation starts without a goal, scope, and validation target.

workflow.name: Frame
workflow.output: Bounded scope, non-goals, dependencies, risks, and rollback.
workflow.gate: Canonical repository ownership and public/private boundary are known.

workflow.name: Assign
workflow.output: One accountable role, supporting reviewers, and an approved file scope.
workflow.gate: One writer per change package; reviewers do not self-promote to writers.

workflow.name: Produce
workflow.output: Code, design, schema, documentation, test, or architecture artifact.
workflow.gate: Only scoped, reversible, evidence-oriented work is accepted.

workflow.name: Review
workflow.output: Quality, security, accessibility, and risk findings.
workflow.gate: Required gates pass or remain explicitly blocked.

workflow.name: Evidence
workflow.output: Commands, results, artifacts, limitations, and remaining gaps.
workflow.gate: No completion claim without current, relevant evidence.

workflow.name: Handoff
workflow.output: Review-ready package, rollback, next decision, and human approval queue.
workflow.gate: External writes, deployment, publication, credentials, and destructive work remain human-gated.

stopAndAskWhen: The requested output changes the project identity or repository boundary.
The required validation environment is unknown and a safe local validator cannot be chosen.
A destructive, external, credential, deployment, publication, or paid-provider action is required.

humanApprovalRequiredFor: SSH, VPN, cloud, or deployment mutation
paid benchmarks, downloads, or external training

initialBacklog.title: Use the agency brief for the next SEIS request
initialBacklog.acceptance: The next brief names scope, non-goals, owner, reviewers, validation, risks, and rollback.

initialBacklog.title: Run one bounded brief through pod assignment
initialBacklog.acceptance: Exactly one accountable role and at least one review gate are recorded without granting new runtime authority.

initialBacklog.title: Pilot an accessible Command Center experience brief
initialBacklog.acceptance: The output includes responsive, keyboard, focus, contrast, reduced-motion, and evidence requirements.

initialBacklog.title: Pilot an AI or knowledge brief with explicit truth boundaries
initialBacklog.acceptance: Provider status, privacy class, evaluation path, fallback, and non-claims are recorded.

initialBacklog.title: Review the first agency package and update the roster
initialBacklog.acceptance: Validation, risks, blockers, rollback, and next decision are captured after the pilot.
